reports.title: Kingsoft Cloud Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 40% to RMB3.48bn, above estimates, on AI cloud demand; record adjusted operating margin but still a net loss; no formal guidance

numbers.eps_basis: diluted GAAP, per ordinary share (1 ADS = 15 shares)

other.label: Adjusted net loss
other.change: vs RMB28.7m profit a year ago

results: Revenue rose 40.4% to RMB3.48bn (13% up on the quarter), the fastest growth in five years and above the RMB3.33bn estimate.
Public cloud grew 57% to RMB2.76bn, driven by AI cloud billings of RMB1.68bn (+115%); enterprise cloud was flat at RMB721m.
Gross margin was 15.5% (adjusted 15.7%); operating profit reached RMB47.9m against a RMB145.3m loss a year ago, with an adjusted operating margin of 4.4%.
Net loss widened to RMB118.1m from RMB7.8m, as interest expense rose to RMB205m and last year had one-off subsidies.
Operating cash flow of RMB6.19bn covered quarterly cash capex of about RMB6.2bn; cash ended at RMB6.20bn.

guidance.summary: Kingsoft Cloud gives no formal revenue or profit guidance. On the call it said nine-month capex of RMB14.7bn is close to its RMB15bn base case for 2026, and it is aiming for a positive adjusted net profit in 2027.

items.new: Base case about RMB15bn (RMB14.7bn spent in 9 months)

points: CEO Tao Zou credited AI demand from third-party platforms and AI labs; AI billings outside the Xiaomi and Kingsoft group grew 120%.
Expiring AI cloud contracts were repriced to current market rates, which the CFO expects to support margins.
Revenue from the Xiaomi and Kingsoft ecosystem was about RMB920m (+33%), 26% of total revenue.
Management said it has no overseas computing and does not expect a significant hit from chip export rules; it is widening sourcing, including domestic chips.
The CFO said capex mix and funding are still under review, with about RMB25bn of undrawn credit lines; interest costs drove the net loss.
call.source: Call transcript: The Motley Fool, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Whether repricing and scale lift margins enough to offset rising depreciation and interest costs.
Capex and funding plans for 2027, and progress toward the positive adjusted net profit target.
Chip supply and export rules, and whether enterprise cloud returns to growth.
